design.fundingOptIn: The advertiser may set aiRelease: true when creating the campaign; the opt-in is immutable once set and per-campaign only.
design.review: The existing AI proof review is unchanged as a record: offchain proofReviews/$escrowId, function-written, participant-readable, capped at 10 runs. An initial attempt to move it onchain so escrow rules could read the verdict was reverted: the platform requires onchain collections to read 'true' (public), and, decisively, a function's ctx.bounded.set cannot sign, so its onchain writes never land (bounded-onchain docs, Poofnet section).
design.rule: New escrow action branch aiRelease in policy.json (generated by scripts/generate-policy.mjs): status submitted, proof present, funding-time aiRelease opt-in, AGENT_ADDRESS_BOUND, actor exactly @const.AGENT_ADDRESS, attestation on the action document (verdict == 'meets-terms', reviewProofUrl == the exact submitted proof, reviewRun 1-10, reviewReviewedAt after submission and not in the future), at least AI_RELEASE_DELAY_SECONDS (21600, 6 hours) after proof submission, and escrow balance. The advertiser's own release, refund and the arbitrator's dispute settlement are unchanged.
design.execution: scripts/ai-release-sweep.mjs runs on the pinned agent's CLI identity: it lists escrows, re-checks every condition, reads the actual offchain review and acts only on a real, fresh, matching meets-terms record, copies that review verbatim into the public onchain attestation, makes one single-use attempt, and requires the successful hook marker (_hook_completed == _transaction_hash, completed true) plus the authoritative head state (status released, version + 1, resolvedBy == agent). No automatic retry of ambiguous actions.
design.trustBoundary: An onchain rule cannot read the offchain review record, so the rules verify the attestation's shape and every onchain-visible condition, but cannot verify the attestation tells the truth. Honesty rests on the pinned agent's release pass copying only real matching reviews; every AI release is publicly auditable because the action document (read 'true') carries the verdict, run, review time and exact proof URL it relied on, and the campaign parties can compare it against the review record they can read. A fully rule-verified AI release needs a platform path for function-signed onchain verdicts. Documented in docs/escrow.md.
